conceptZh: 玩具機器人翻著一本厚書越看越入迷，頭一點一點地開始打瞌睡，書慢慢滑下來蓋在他臉上；他就這樣睡著發出小小的呼聲，每呼一次就有一頁被吹得掀起來又落下。
object: a small toy robot and a thick picture book
morph: the glyph 書 stands still as a solid sculpture while the robot falls asleep under the book
creativeAngle: 孩子看漫畫看到睡著是很有共鳴的畫面，笑點用「每呼一次就掀一頁」的小細節收尾，安靜卻很好笑，也和其他支的大動作形成節奏對比。書為聿在上、曰在下共十畫，橫畫多容易糊，字體靜止並要求橫畫等距。語音詞「看書」，看在此念ㄎㄢˋ、書ㄕㄨ，避開照看的ㄎㄢ。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale butter cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 書 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep navy, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the brush-shaped 聿 on top sits above the 曰 below, clearly separated, with every horizontal stroke evenly spaced and never merging. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. At its base sits a small boxy toy robot with a thick picture book open on his knees. From 0.5 seconds he reads with real interest, turning a page, leaning in. At 1.4 seconds his head dips, and snaps back up. He blinks hard and carries on. At 2.0 seconds it dips again, lower, and comes back up more slowly. At 2.6 seconds his arms sag and the book slides gently up over his face and settles there like a little tent. He does not move. Beat. From 3.2 seconds, tiny soft snores begin, and with each one a single page lifts up off the book and drops back down, in a slow steady rhythm. Hold on that quiet joke through 4.2 seconds, then the sleeping robot and his book slide gently out of frame to the left by 4.6 seconds. From 4.7 seconds to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 書 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「書、書、看書」, using the reading ㄕㄨ for 書 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 書 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 看書 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 書: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 披風英雄的長披風跟著他翻書的動作，慢一拍就把書頁攪亂，最後書頁剛好疊成「書」。
object: caped action-figure hero, an oversized cape, a thick storybook
morph: flying pages settle into the strokes of 書
creativeAngle: 披風慢一拍模仿主角每個動作，造成翻頁的小混亂。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy, locked frontal camera. Setting: a warm coral reading nook with a pale-cream floor; the glyph is deep forest-green paper-craft strokes standing at center. A caped action-figure hero (an original toy with a plain teal cape three sizes too long) stands at right holding a thick book. The Traditional Chinese glyph 書 stays centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the hero opens the big book with a flourish, and a beat later the cape flips open too and flops over his head; the first 書 is spoken as the cover opens. Moment two (1.8-3.5s): he flips a page and the cape flips one beat late, whipping pages into the air; they flutter, fold and snap into the horizontal bars and vertical strokes of 書 at center; the second 書 is spoken as the final page lands. Moment three (3.5-5.0s): he tries to look cool, but the cape sweeps a small school bag off a shelf onto his shoulders; 書包 is spoken as the bag lands with a soft bounce. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 書 is perfectly still and unobstructed; the cape still mimics each pose a beat late: he points, then the cape points; the glyph is untouched. Audio: one warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in Taiwan-standard Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 「書、書、書包」 (ㄕㄨ、ㄕㄨ、ㄕㄨ ㄅㄠ). Timing: first utterance at about 0.5s, second at about 2.5s, the word at about 4.4s; then stop, no repeats and no extra speech. Beneath the voice only page flutters and cloth swishes, no music. The single glyph is the only on-screen text; the vocabulary stays audio-only with no subtitles, watermark, clutter or flashing.
